Dark - Astrup - Midsummer Eve Bonfire.jp.about: Astrup painted the Midsummer bonfires of his home village, Jølster, many times as paintings and woodcuts. Here a lone dark figure stands against the flames while the other villagers gather on the slope beyond. He worked on this version in 1912 and again in 1926.
Dark - Astrup - Midsummer Eve Bonfire.jp.title: Bonfire celebrating Midsummer Night

Dark - Homer - Moonlight, Wood Island Li.about: Moonlit surf on the rocks at Prouts Neck, Maine, where Homer had his studio. The red dot on the horizon is the Wood Island lighthouse. His first biographer said Homer ran to the shore one summer night on impulse and painted it in four or five hours.
Dark - Homer - Moonlight, Wood Island Li.title: Moonlight, Wood Island Light
Dark - Homer - Moonlight, Wood Island Li.where: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

Dark - Munch - Starry Night.jpg.about: The shoreline at Åsgårdstrand, the small Norwegian beach town where Munch spent his summers, under a deep blue night sky. He was trying to paint the feelings the night stirred up rather than a faithful picture of the view.
Dark - Munch - Starry Night.jpg.title: Starry Night
Dark - Munch - Starry Night.jpg.where: J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles

Dark - Pissarro - Boulevard Montmartre a.about: In 1897 Pissarro painted 14 views of this Paris boulevard from a hotel room above it, and this is his only night scene. The cool white of new electric streetlamps contrasts with the yellow gaslight of shop windows, all reflected on the wet pavement.
Dark - Pissarro - Boulevard Montmartre a.title: The Boulevard Montmartre at Night

Dark - Ury - Nollendorfplatz at Night.jp.about: Ury kept a top-floor studio at Nollendorfplatz 1 in Berlin from 1901 until his death and painted the square below for three decades. Here the elevated station is a dark silhouette as a lit train pulls in and people walk toward us.
Dark - Ury - Nollendorfplatz at Night.jp.title: Nollendorfplatz Station at Night (Bahnhof Nollendorfplatz bei Nacht)

Light - Bierstadt - Among the Sierra Nev.about: An idealized Sierra Nevada valley with a waterfall, a still lake, and deer. Bierstadt painted it in Europe and toured it through European cities before shipping it to America. He unveiled his huge canvases like theater, in darkened rooms behind drawn curtains.
Light - Bierstadt - Among the Sierra Nev.title: Among the Sierra Nevada, California
Light - Bierstadt - Among the Sierra Nev.where: Smithsonian American Art Museum, Washington, D.C.

Light - Corot - The Bridge at Narni.jpg.about: The ruined Roman bridge of Augustus over the Nera river at Narni, north of Rome. Corot painted this oil sketch on paper in September 1826, on his first trip to Italy. He used it for a larger, more finished version shown at the 1827 Salon.
Light - Corot - The Bridge at Narni.jpg.title: The Bridge at Narni

Light - Cropsey - Autumn on the Hudson R.about: The Hudson River Valley in full fall color, looking toward Storm King Mountain. Cropsey painted it from memory in his London studio. British viewers doubted American leaves could be so red, so he displayed real ones next to the painting.
Light - Cropsey - Autumn on the Hudson R.title: Autumn - On the Hudson River
Light - Cropsey - Autumn on the Hudson R.where: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C.

Light - Inness - Peace and Plenty.jpg.about: A broad harvest landscape with stacked sheaves of wheat under a golden sky, finished near the end of the Civil War. The title and the bountiful harvest express Inness's confidence in a Union victory and the prosperity to follow.
Light - Inness - Peace and Plenty.jpg.title: Peace and Plenty
Light - Inness - Peace and Plenty.jpg.where: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

Light - Levitan - Golden Autumn, Slobodk.about: A village of log huts on an autumn day, with one young birch in bright yellow leaf among the fenced plots. The birch is the brightest patch of color in the picture and ties together the muted greens and browns around it.
Light - Levitan - Golden Autumn, Slobodk.title: Golden Autumn. Slobodka

Light - Levitan - March.jpg.about: Bright spring sun on melting snow beside a wooden house, with a horse and sledge waiting by the porch. Levitan painted it in March 1895 while staying at the Gorka estate in Tver province. Pavel Tretyakov bought it from him the next year.
Light - Levitan - March.jpg.title: March

Light - Monet - Stacks of Wheat, End of.about: Two tall wheat stacks just outside Monet's farmhouse at Giverny in late summer light. He painted the series at several easels at once as the light changed. Fifteen were hung together in Paris in 1891, a big critical and financial success.
Light - Monet - Stacks of Wheat, End of.title: Stacks of Wheat (End of Summer)

Light - Monet - Sunset on the Seine at L.about: The sun sets over the Seine at Lavacourt after the harsh winter of 1879–80, when the frozen river thawed. Monet painted this freer canvas alongside a more conventional one for the 1880 Salon. The museum believes this is the one the jury rejected.
Light - Monet - Sunset on the Seine at L.title: Sunset on the Seine at Lavacourt, Winter Effect

Light - Monet - The Magpie.jpg.about: A single magpie perches on a gate in fresh snow near Étretat, with blue shadows across the white. Monet painted it on the spot in the winter of 1868–69. Its pale, bright colors startled people, and the 1869 Salon jury rejected it.
Light - Monet - The Magpie.jpg.title: The Magpie

Light - Monet - Water Lilies.jpg.about: Lily pads and yellow blossoms float on Monet's pond at Giverny, with the sky reflected between them. The painter Torajirō Kojima visited Monet and bought it directly from him for collector Magosaburō Ōhara. It is a founding work of Japan's first museum of Western art.
Light - Monet - Water Lilies.jpg.title: Waterlilies

Light - Sisley - Banks of the Loing, Aut.about: The Loing river curves below a hillside near Veneux-Nadon, painted in Sisley's second autumn there. Bare trees frame the view and two small figures work in the field. Looted in World War II, it came to the museum through a postwar Jewish restitution organization.
Light - Sisley - Banks of the Loing, Aut.title: Banks of the Loing — Autumn Effect

Light - Turner - Modern Rome, Campo Vacc.about: The Roman Forum, then half-buried and known as the Campo Vaccino or cow pasture, glowing in hazy light. It was Turner's last painting of Rome, made from memory. The Getty bought it at auction in 2010 for a record price for a Turner.
Light - Turner - Modern Rome, Campo Vacc.title: Modern Rome - Campo Vaccino
Light - Turner - Modern Rome, Campo Vacc.where: J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles

Light - Turner - Rain, Steam and Speed.j.about: A steam train rushes toward us across Brunel's Maidenhead Railway Bridge in the rain. Turner painted a hare running along the track to set nature's speed against the machine's. The paint has turned transparent with age, and the hare is now nearly invisible.
Light - Turner - Rain, Steam and Speed.j.title: Rain, Steam, and Speed - The Great Western Railway

Light - Vermeer - View of Delft.jpg.about: Vermeer's hometown seen across the harbor on a calm morning, under drifting clouds. He tidied the real skyline and shifted the sunlit tower of the New Church toward the center. Marcel Proust called it the most beautiful painting in the world.
Light - Vermeer - View of Delft.jpg.title: View of Delft

Light - Whistler - Nocturne Blue and Sil.about: The Thames at dusk looking toward Chelsea, with a barge and a lone figure on the foreshore. It was the first of Whistler's nocturnes. He borrowed musical terms for his titles because he saw a painting as an arrangement of colors, like notes in music.
Light - Whistler - Nocturne Blue and Sil.title: Nocturne: Blue and Silver - Chelsea
